PARIS and SAINT-ROMAIN-AU-MONT-D'OR, France, Nov. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Within the framework of the statutory publication of its Q3 2026 revenue, Artmarket.com—whose Artprice department has been the World Leader in Art Market databanks since its creation in 1997, nearly 30 years ago—announces the global beta-test rollout in early December 2026 of Artprice Visual Search® (registered trademark), followed in January 2027 by its commercial launch within its high-end Premium and high-end Professional subscriptions. Artprice by Artmarket - Artprice Visual Search® The culmination of several years of research and development led by thierry Ehrmann and his teams of engineers, data scientists, and art historians, this proprietary and vertical artificial intelligence marks a fundamental milestone in Artprice's "AI-First" architecture. Whereas the dozens, or even hundreds, of artwork recognition experiments attempted across the world until now relied on deep learning limited to 10,000, 12,000, or 20,000 images with very little metadata documentation, Artprice Visual Search® achieves a true quantum leap by processing several terabytes of high-definition images and metadata certified over nearly 30 years by its historians and editors on the works referenced in its databanks. Rollout schedule and strong pricing leverage starting January 2027: To maximize global adoption and the financial impact of this technological breakthrough on the Art Market, Artprice by Artmarket.com is rolling out Artprice Visual Search® according to a two-stage industrial strategy: Early December 2026 – Opening of the beta version to all Artprice clients: Throughout the entire month of December 2026, Artprice is granting its entire global subscriber base access to the beta version of Artprice Visual Search®. This strategic opening allows each client to measure, under real-world conditions, the investigative and valuation power of the tool on their own research and collections. Starting January 2027 – Commercial launch within high-end Premium and Professional offers at significantly higher rates: As of January 2027, Artprice Visual Search® will be integrated into the high-end Premium and high-end Professional subscription plans, accompanied—in full economic logic given the added value delivered—by significantly higher rates. The beta access offered in December 2026 thus acts as a powerful conversion accelerator to drive existing clients to switch massively starting in January 2027 toward these high-contribution subscriptions, generating a structural increase in average revenue per user (ARPU). 30 years of "AI-First" doctrine: from Intuitive Artmarket® and Blind Spot® to the quantum leap of Artprice Visual Search® Since its founding in 1997—nearly 30 years of uninterrupted investment—Artprice has built its near-global hegemony on proprietary database engineering (now covering 930,000 artists and auction traceability since 1700), refusing any external technological dependency in order to prepare for the advent of a purely vertical and proprietary artificial intelligence dedicated to the Art Market. Even before the rest of the sector measured the impact of foundation models, Artprice by Artmarket.com deployed its AI-First ecosystem: Intuitive Artmarket®: Artprice's generalist, proprietary, and strictly vertical AI, capable of analyzing in real time the econometric, biographical, and historical complexity of the entire global Art Market. Blind Spot®: Artprice's predictive and analytical algorithm designed to detect the blind spots of the Art Market, identify weak signals, and reveal undervaluations or correlations invisible to the human eye. Artprice Visual Search® (Beta early December 2026 / Premium & Professional Offers January 2027): The most advanced building block of this architecture. Because the image constitutes the most complex and universal cognitive structure in art, Artprice Visual Search® propels Artprice's computing power into the direct analysis of visual matter across several terabytes of archives of reproductions and documentation of works of art, equipped with a self-learning engine that continuously enriches and refines itself. Statement by thierry Ehrmann, Founder of Artprice and CEO of Artmarket.com: "With the global beta-test rollout of Artprice Visual Search® in early December 2026, followed in January 2027 by its commercial launch within our high-end Premium and Professional offers, our 30 years of AI-First strategy since the creation of Artprice in 1997 reach their natural crowning achievement. After laying the cognitive and econometric foundations of the sector with Intuitive Artmarket®—our generalist, proprietary, and vertical AI—and then unveiling the weak signals and blind spots of the Art Market thanks to the unseen gaze of Blind Spot®, we are today taking a true quantum leap: that of purely visual intelligence applied to several terabytes of data and an unrivalled collection of nearly 145 million images of works of art. Our search capability on works of art referenced by Artprice is superior to generalist engines that run up against the mathematical limits of simple pattern recognition: Artprice's proprietary RAG architecture cross-references the visual fingerprint of the reproduction with its certified historical metadata, ensuring optimal identification accuracy and reducing the margin of visual uncertainty to a statistically marginal level. Why does it succeed while continuously improving at the algorithmic level, where the dozens, or even hundreds, of artwork recognition experiments conducted around the world have failed? Because a very large proportion of those vertical applications relied until now on embryonic deep learning limited to 10,000, 12,000, or 15,000 images, which were moreover very poorly documented. Yet the naked pixel is blind if it is not irrigated by the historical memory of the Art Market. By training our proprietary AI on 23 million reproductions of works of art annotated over nearly 30 years by our historians, editors, econometricians, and documentalists, with 180 structured and completed fields for each reproduction of a work of art, we have endowed Artprice Visual Search® with a true cerebral image. This is where database science meets aesthetic philosophy. I have worked extensively on the work of Luigi Pareyson and his theory of formativity*—the forming form (forma formante), that movement through which the work invents its own formal law in the very act of being created. It is this approach which, thanks to the power of the Artprice Visual Search® AI, will make it possible to push back the academic limits of the human-based Art Market toward new horizons where only the computing power of our AI can scientifically and reliably detect these new forms that will metamorphose the history of Art and, by extension, its Market. Today, hundreds of millions of collectors and enthusiasts are no longer looking merely for a signature or a subject: they are searching for aesthetic powers, forms, color strata, supports/surfaces, and mediums. *(In summary, the creator does not impose an abstract idea onto matter: he engages in a dialogue with his work in the making, and it is the work itself—acting as a forming form—that reveals to him how it must be constructed through a process of formativity.) We are light-years ahead of the archaic algorithmic model of the 2010s inherited from Amazon ("those who viewed this artist also viewed this"). By instantaneously returning 49 works qualified by percentage degree of relevance, Artprice Visual Search® connects the $2,000 Dutch Vanitas and the $170,000 museum-grade masterpiece within a single plastic continuity, while preserving the power of the Art Market's high returns, which range between 14% and 15% above $100,000. By opening this beta version to all our clients in early December so that they can transition in January 2027 to our high-end Premium and Professional subscriptions, we are shattering the locks of a historically rigid and academic Art Market. Let us recall that it took Artprice 5 to 6 years of continuous effort to establish worldwide the very notions of Contemporary Art—artists born after 1945—and Ultra-Contemporary Art—under 40 years old on a rolling basis—and that it still takes 5, 10, or even 15 years today for art dealers (who have replaced the Academy), sociologists, critics, and art historians to formally identify a new school. Thanks to Artprice Visual Search®, backed by our historic alliance of over 25 years with the PR Newswire / Cision group, we will now uncover and reveal in real time, in a rigorously scientific and academic manner, hundreds of new movements, new forms, and new meanings across the world." The quantum leap compared to global trials: 30 years of historical annotation across 23 million images (180 fields) on works referenced by Artprice Until today, the dozens, or even hundreds, of attempts at visual recognition of works of art launched by laboratories or technology players around the world have all hit the same glass ceiling: they invariably relied on deep learning restricted to 10,000, 12,000, or 15,000 images, suffering moreover from virtually non-existent or superficial historical documentation from the Art Market. With Artprice Visual Search®, Artprice by Artmarket.com shifts to a new industrial and scientific scale: Training on 23 million annotated reproductions resulting from nearly 30 years of work by historians (nearly 2,000 times the size of conventional samples): Artprice's proprietary AI was trained on a hard core of 23 million images of works of art fully documented, qualified, and verified since 1997—nearly 30 years of work and research by Artprice's historians and experts—before being deployed across the global collection reaching nearly 145 million images currently being processed. 180 documentary fields per reproduction of a work of art: For each image analyzed, the AI mobilizes and cross-references 180 structured fields (provenance, school, technique, supports/surfaces, mediums, signatures and monograms, dimensions, auction history since 1700, catalogue raisonné references, iconography, internal geometry, chromatic strata). This matrix density makes it the most intelligent and best-modeled AI in the world for recognizing a work of art in a complete and absolute manner. Where generalist engines run up against the mathematical limits of simple pattern recognition, Artprice's proprietary RAG architecture cross-references the visual fingerprint of the reproduction with its certified historical metadata, ensuring optimal identification accuracy and reducing the margin of visual uncertainty to a statistically marginal level. Thanks to this fusion between computer vision and archival truth across its sovereign scope of over 930,000 artists, Artprice Visual Search® immediately achieves remarkable execution purity on works of art referenced by Artprice, while benefiting from a continuous algorithmic optimization loop with every new query and data integration. A matrix output of 49 works by correlation index: For any submitted work, the tool instantaneously delivers 49 matching works assigned a precise relevance percentage—whether works by the same artist (immediately identified from the very first image) or matches in themes, formal structures, and exact or complementary colorimetries. Sociological and anthropological vision: how the 30–45 generation (America, Europe, Greater Asia) "bypasses" ostentatious and pageant luxury in favor of collecting as an intellectual "backbone" Beyond the technological breakthrough, Artprice Visual Search® is the fruit of a sociological, and even anthropological, study conducted over several years by thierry Ehrmann and his teams across America, Europe, and Greater Asia. Artprice has indeed identified a vast pool of new collectors aged 30 to 45, permanently connected day and night to the Internet, who have mentally structured a completely different architecture in their approach to values and to what a work of art can deliver aesthetically: Early success built through genius and relentless hard work: Having started very early and built their fortunes very young by working day and night, these decision-makers—with a passion for culture and notably digital art—have already moved beyond the whims of a bygone era. They categorically refuse to be mistaken for mere stereotypical young millionaires. The deliberate "bypass" of ostentatious and pageant luxury: Rather than losing their way in traditional high-luxury circuits—such as luxury cars—they deliberately choose to bypass ostentatious, pageant luxury, which in their eyes constitutes a waste of time and a risk that turns the individual into a consumption machine and a walking target. The collection as an intellectual "backbone" (chemin de fer) defining a man, a woman, a household: They go straight to the essential by asserting their maturity and social success through their intellectual investment. When a 35-year-old collector or couple presents their collection—built far from conventional classics around a true guiding thread, a cerebral backbone (chemin de fer) that demonstrates what they see and the values they carry within—the rigor of their approach immediately commands admiration. Finding what is humanly impossible to search for: In search of aesthetic powers, forms (Luigi Pareyson's forming form*), color strata, supports/surfaces, and mediums of their own, these collectors with sharp and deeply considered choices are creating new movements that the traditional dealer world struggles to grasp for lack of AI tools and computing power. Artprice Visual Search® provides them with the indispensable cerebral image to uncover, among nearly 145 million images, the exact works they are looking for—an exploration that was until now humanly impossible to achieve. Decompartmentalizing a rigid and academic Art Market: from the "Ultra-Contemporary" precedent to the scientific discovery of hundreds of movements broadcast across 125 countries and in 14 languages The traditional Art Market has historically suffered from a rigid, academic framework and heavy conceptual inertia. It was Artprice that created and globally established the econometric categories of "Contemporary Art" and "Ultra-Contemporary Art," yet it took 5 to 6 years of continuous effort to lastingly implant this essential standard into the mindset of the global Art Market. Similarly, art dealers—who have progressively replaced the Academy—much like sociologists, art critics, and historians, typically take 10 to 15 years (and a minimum of 5 years in exceptional cases) to formally discern new forms, new schools, or new aesthetic meanings capable of destabilizing the organization of the Art Market and its economy. Thanks to the pure acceleration inherent to its AI, Artprice Visual Search® shatters these disciplinary locks in real time: The scientific and academic emergence of hundreds of movements: By instantaneously cross-referencing morphologies, supports/surfaces, mediums, and chromatic strata off the beaten path, Artprice's AI makes it possible to uncover—in a rigorously scientific and academic manner—hundreds of movements, schools, and plastic lineages that had until now remained in the shadows of the Art Market. A global sounding board across 125 countries and in 14 languages with the PR Newswire / Cision group—with which Artprice by Artmarket.com is currently finalizing an exceptional, even more powerful new strategic agreement—Artprice broadcasts its analyses and discoveries through its multiple networks. These new movements and new aesthetic approaches will thus benefit from immediate planetary recognition, irreversibly reshaping the strata of the Art Market. From the $2,000 Vanitas to $170,000 masterpieces on the same theme: uniting the high returns of the Art Market with hundreds of millions of enthusiasts The universality of Artprice Visual Search® enables it to act simultaneously on both poles of the Art Market: high financial performance and accessibility to the greatest number. Above the $100,000 threshold, works of art on the Art Market generate a particularly robust average annual return of between 14% and 15%. Yet the vocation of Artprice Visual Search® is to go far beyond this financial elite alone to reach hundreds of millions of art collectors and enthusiasts who organize their collections around a theme, a color stratum, a medium, or a search for forms, with the desire both to enhance the coherence of their holdings and, where applicable, to resell on the Art Market with a significant return on investment. The concrete example of Vanitas paintings: An art lover searching for Vanitas works via Artprice Visual Search® can identify very fine Dutch School Vanitas paintings around $2,000, while being offered, within the exact same formal and colorimetric continuity, a major Vanitas at $170,000 boasting museum-grade standing and competing fully in the upper echelons of the Art Market. By offering beta access to this visual revolution to all its clients starting in early December 2026, ahead of the January 2027 launch of its new high-end Premium and high-end Professional offers, Artprice by Artmarket.com abolishes the boundary between pure plastic research, the anthropology of new global collectors, and the econometric intelligence of the Art Market, while opening a major value-creation cycle for its shareholders. articles.title: Nvidia's value plummets by £200bn as amount equal to entire NHS budget wiped after CEO's affair with alleged spy
articles.description: The share price of US tech giant Nvidia has plummeted by around £200billion after the CEO's affair with an alleged Chinese spy - the same value of the entire NHS budget. Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials suspect of passing sensitive information to Beijing. This morning, shares in one of the world's most valuable companies took a nosedive of up to six per cent, which amounts to roughly £200billion. Nvidia is one of the globe's leading firms, and has become a key player in the hardware for new AI technologies. The drop is a devastating blow to the unfaithful CEO, who has overseen the £3.4trillion firm for three decades. Mr Huang is currently at the centre of an independent probe, launched yesterday, to find out whether the CEO had been targeted in an intelligence plot. Announcing the investigation, a statement from the tech firm read: "The Board prioritises US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders. "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information." The AI boss previously admitted his infidelity to Nvidia employees, and said apologised for hurting his family. He said: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. "Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. "I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American." LATEST US NEWS: Nvidia boss admits affair with suspected Chinese spy as probe launched into espionage claims ‘China is going to win the AI race’ says Nvidia boss in stark warning over US tech rivalry Nvidia debuts revolutionary self-driving technology with goals for 'every single car' to be autonomous Donald Trump said he had not spoken to the CEO since the affair was exposed. Speaking to reporters, the US President lauded Mr Huang for doing an "amazing job" for America, adding: "I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what's going on." Last month, it was reported that Mr Trump had been informed of the possible intelligence threat. When asked whether he should have acted more quickly on the matter, the President doubled down on his stance. "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honourable guy," he said. Discussing the scandal this morning, Shadow Foreign Secretary Tom Tugendhat told the BBC "it wouldn't at all surprise" him if Beijing only enlisted Ms Huang after the affair began. He said it "would not be beyond the Chinese state" to threaten imprisoning her family if she refused to engage in the intelligence effort. China has denied allegations of enlisting Ms Huang as an intelligence asset, dubbing the accusations "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China". articles.title: DeFi Development Corp. Increases SOL Treasury to 2.61 Million
articles.description: Company Adds 8,881 SOL and SOL Equivalents, Marking Nine Consecutive Weeks of SOL Purchases CHAD's 14.00% annual dividend rate continues to offer one of the most competitive income opportunities in digital credit BOCA RATON, FL, Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- DeFi Development Corp. (Nasdaq: DFDV) (the "Company" or "DeFi Dev Corp."), the first U.S. public company with a treasury strategy built to accumulate and compound Solana ("SOL"), today announced that its total holdings of SOL and SOL equivalents increased by 8,881 SOL since its last update, bringing its treasury to approximately 2,609,829 SOL, up from 2,600,948 SOL. The increase marks the Company's ninth consecutive week of SOL purchases since September 14, 2026, building on its return to active accumulation on August 27. The continued purchases reflect the Company's continued execution of its treasury strategy, focused on growing SOL holdings and increasing SOL per share ("SPS") over time. "Our strategy remains consistent: accumulate SOL, compound our holdings, and grow SOL per share,” said Joseph Onorati, Chief Executive Officer of DeFi Development Corp. "We remain focused on disciplined execution and positioning the Company to create long-term shareholder value as the Solana ecosystem continues to develop.” CHAD Continues to Offer One of the Highest Dividend Rates in Digital Credit DeFi Development Corp.'s Variable Rate Series C Perpetual Preferred Stock (Nasdaq: CHAD) continues to offer a 14.00% annualized dividend rate, among the highest in the digital credit market. Based on its $10.00 stated amount, CHAD's 14.00% annualized dividend rate equates to $1.40 per share annually. Dividends are cumulative and payable each business day when, as and if declared by the Company's Board of Directors. CHAD offers income-focused investors a differentiated way to participate in the Company's SOL treasury strategy. Unlike traditional corporate treasuries, which typically hold cash and other low-yielding assets, DeFi Development Corp.'s SOL holdings can generate recurring income through native staking and validator operations. The Company believes this productive treasury provides a strong foundation for scaling its digital credit offerings. "CHAD combines a 14% annualized dividend rate with a treasury of productive SOL assets, creating what we believe is a compelling proposition for income-focused investors,” said Onorati. "As we grow CHAD, our objective is to expand our capacity to accumulate SOL while continuing to drive long-term SOL per share growth for common shareholders.” The Company intends to continue growing CHAD as a core component of its long-term capital strategy, providing income-focused investors with an alternative to common equity while supporting continued SOL accumulation. Learn more about CHAD at www.defidevcorp.com/chad. For more information, visit defidevcorp.com. To stay up to date with the latest developments and insights, subscribe to our blog. articles.title: Sonoro Intersects 1.13 g/t Au over 19.81 Meters at Historical El Batamote Mine and Expands Mineralization at Diana with 0.82 g/t Au over 50.3 Meters
articles.description: VANCOUVER, Canada, Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sonoro Gold Corp. (TSXV: SGO | OTCQB: SMOFF | FRA: 23SP) ("Sonoro" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that drilling has extended near-surface gold mineralization at Diana and intersected gold-silver mineralization beneath the historic El Batamote mine. The Company has now completed 104 reverse circulation ("RC") drill holes totaling 21,345.12 meters as part of its ongoing 50,000-meter exploration drilling program at the Company’s flagship Cerro Caliche gold project in Sonora, Mexico. HIGHLIGHTS Diana Mineralization Extended: Step-out holes collared up to approximately 245 meters ("m”) east to southeast of the previously announced higher-grade SCR-387 drill hole extended mineralization with all 21 new drill holes returning gold above the cut-off. Near surface mineralization began within the first 30m downhole in 20 of the 21 drill holes. SCR-399 intercepted 9.15m @ 1.286 g/t Au, including 4.57m @ 2.366 g/t AuSCR-404 intercepted 50.30m @ 0.823 g/t Au, including 1.52m @ 9.372 g/t AuSCR-422 intercepted 50.29m @ 0.513 g/t Au, including 6.09m @ 2.038 g/t AuEl Batamote Gold-Silver Intercepts: Initial five drill holes below the historical workings intersected high-grade gold-silver mineralization, indicative of higher level epithermal-style mineralization often seen above high-grade feeder veins.SCR-406 intercepted 19.81m @ 1.127 g/t Au and 15.1 g/t Ag, including 4.57m @ 2.350 g/t Au and 12.7 g/t AgSCR-409 intercepted 15.24m @ 0.713 g/t Au and 10.1 g/t Ag, including 3.04m @ 1.769 g/t Au and 28.4 g/t Ag The recently acquired Diana and El Batamote concessions are located approximately two kilometers ("km”) north of the proposed open-pit, heap leach mining operation as outlined in a Preliminary Economic Assessment (the "PEA”) filed April 24, 2026. Results from 21 drill holes completed at Diana and five drill holes completed at El Batamote support the Company's strategy of acquiring and systematically exploring prospective ground surrounding Cerro Caliche's current mineral resources. "Drilling at Diana continues to build upon our previous higher-grade gold intercepts and improve our understanding of the mineralized corridors extending northward from El Rincón and Bellotoso. Results at El Batamote support the interpreted continuation of these corridors across the post-mineral fault into our recently acquired northern concessions,” said Sonoro President & CEO Kenneth MacLeod. "All 26 holes in this release intersected gold mineralization, with mineralized intervals starting within the first 30 meters downhole in 22 of them. These results reinforce our decision to acquire and explore this ground. The mineralization reported here is not included in the mine plan evaluated in our current PEA but offers potential for future resource growth, subject to further exploration and technical evaluation. We remain focused on advancing permitting for Cerro Caliche, and we have only begun to explore the concessions acquired in 2026.” The map below illustrates the proposed mine footprint, including the open pits, the original 1,350-hectare property boundary, the Diana concession, interpreted mineralized corridors, and mapped and projected faults. Drill hole locations are differentiated by category. Figure 1: Cerro Caliche Gold Project Please click to view image Mineralized Corridors In the northern part of the Cerro Caliche project, a northeast-trending post-mineral fault separates the Bellotoso-Diana plateau from El Batamote located at the foot of the plateau. The El Batamote block is interpreted to have been downthrown relative to the plateau, and this structural setting suggests concealed extensions of the gold-bearing vein systems identified at Cerro Caliche and Diana. Further drilling is required to confirm extensions are present at depth, as well as continuity and grade. The plateau is capped by erosion-resistant rhyolite domes. Extensive geological mapping has identified northwest-trending veins, breccias and rhyolite dikes with characteristics similar to those associated with gold mineralization in the proposed open-pit area. The recently completed 26 drill holes investigated two important inquiries at Diana and El Batamote. First, drilling investigated whether the northwest-trending vein corridors at the top of the Diana plateau, located northeast of El Rincón and Bellotoso, represent extensions of the same mineralized structural system. Drilling followed up on the previously reported higher-grade intercepts and included both step-out drilling and tests of mineralization at depth. Second, drilling at El Batamote investigated whether the interpreted extensions of Diana’s mineralized vein corridors across the post-mineral fault and beneath the historic workings at El Batamote host gold mineralization. El Batamote lies approximately 1.2 km west-northwest of Diana, at an elevation approximately 300m lower than the main Diana drilling area. Diana Mineralized Zone At the Diana mineralized zone, the Company completed 21 drill holes over 4,690.84 m confirming the expansion of at or near surface gold mineralization. All 21 holes returned intervals grading at or above the 0.13 g/t Au reporting cut-off, with qualifying intervals starting within the first 30m downhole in 20 of the 21 drill holes. A total of 10 step-out drill holes follow up on previously reported higher-grade drilling results. Drill hole SCR-412 was collared approximately 97m northeast of previously disclosed drill hole SCR-387 which returned 28.95m @ 2.598 g/t Au, including 13.72m @ 5.101 g/t Au, while drill holes SCR-414 to SCR-420 were collared approximately 74 to 245m east to southeast of SCR-387. These distances are horizontal collar-to-collar measurements. SCR-411 and SCR-413 were collared close and at steeper inclinations to SCR-387 and previously disclosed SCR-391 which returned 32m @ 1.846 g/t Au, including 4.57m @ 10.430 g/t Au. Highlights: SCR-419 intercepted 12.20m @ 0.76 g/t Au, including 1.52m @ 4.02 g/t AuSCR-420 intercepted 28.96m @ 0.44 g/t Au, including 3.05m @ 1.45 g/t AuSCR-414 intercepted 21.34m @ 0.50 g/t Au, including 3.05m @ 1.35 g/t AuSCR-418 intercepted 32.00m @ 0.35 g/t Au, from surface to 32.00mSCR-417 intercepted 21.34m @ 0.39 g/t Au, from 1.52 to 22.86m A total of eight drill holes tested the corridors at depth and along strike from 274.32m to 384.05m downhole. Drill hole SCR-404 returned a near-surface interval of 50.30m @ 0.82 g/t Au from 1.52m to 51.82 m, including 1.52m @ 9.37 g/t Au and 8.5 g/t Ag from 30.48m to 32.00m. Drill hole SCR-399 returned 9.15m @ 1.29 g/t Au from 27.43m to 36.58m, including 4.57m @ 2.37 g/t Au from 28.96m to 33.53m, whereas drill hole SCR-421 returned 21.34m @ 0.28 g/t Au from 19.81m to 41.15m. Below approximately 60m downhole, results generally returned shorter mineralized intervals. Notable results include drill hole SCR-402 which returned 3.05m @ 0.93 g/t Au from 190.50m to 193.55m, including 1.52m @ 1.67 g/t Au from 190.50m to 192.02 m, and drill hole SCR-404 which returned 1.53m @ 1.11 g/t Au from 92.96m to 94.49m. These intercepts demonstrate the presence of gold mineralization at depth, but further drilling is required to establish its continuity and test for higher-grade shoots. Drill hole SCR-422 returned 50.29m @ 0.51 g/t Au from 7.62 to 57.91m downhole, including 6.09m @ 2.04 g/t Au from 18.29 to 24.38m. Drill hole SCR-423 returned 85.35m @ 0.33 g/t Au from 16.76m to 102.11m, the longest mineralized interval reported at Diana from the 21 drill holes. El Batamote Mineralized Zone Drilling at the historic El Batamote mine site, located approximately 1.2 km west-northwest of Diana, hosts mineralization interpreted to represent a continuation of the Diana mineralized corridors within a block downthrown by post-mineral faulting. As previously disclosed, the Company acquired data from prior drilling at El Batamote completed by Paget Southern Resources in 2012. The historical data was used to assist in the development of the current RC drilling program at El Batamote. The Company completed five drill holes over 970.78m at the historic workings which all intersected gold-silver mineralization. El Batamote sits at the foot of the Bellotoso-Diana plateau, at an elevation approximately 300m lower than the main Diana drilling area. All five holes returned mineralized intervals within the approximate 45-95m downhole range, with additional intervals intersected at or near surface and at greater downhole depths. Assuming a constant hole inclination of 45°, the 45-95m downhole range corresponds to approximately 32-67m vertically below the respective collar elevations. These vertical distances are referenced to each collar elevation and do not necessarily represent depths below the local topographic surface. Reported mineralized intervals generally demonstrate higher silver-to-gold grade ratios at El Batamote than at Diana, although the ratios vary between intervals. SCR-406 intercepted 19.81m @ 1.13 g/t Au and 15.1 g/t Ag, including 1.52m @ 3.60 g/t Au and 58.5 g/t Ag, and 4.57m @ 2.35 g/t Au and 12.7 g/t AgSCR-409 intercepted 15.24m @ 0.71 g/t Au and 10.1 g/t Ag, including 3.04m @ 1.77 g/t Au and 28.4 g/t AgSCR-408a intercepted 4.58m @ 1.09 g/t Au and 8.5 g/t Ag, including 3.05m @ 1.44 g/t Au and 8.1 g/t Ag, and 3.04m @ 1.67 g/t Au and 6.9 g/t Ag, including 1.52m @ 3.03 g/t Au and 8.5 g/t AgSCR-407 intercepted 7.62m @ 0.41 g/t Au and 0.9 g/t Ag, and 4.57m @ 0.32 g/t Au and 4.0 g/t Ag, and 9.14m @ 0.24 g/t Au and 2.4 g/t AgSCR-408 intercepted 4.57m @ 0.31 g/t Au and 9.3 g/t Ag Results at El Batamote support the interpretation that the Cerro Caliche mineralized corridors extend across the post-mineral fault into the northern concessions. The interpreted downthrown block may host concealed extensions of the vein systems identified at Cerro Caliche and Diana. The higher silver-to-gold ratios reported in parts of El Batamote do not, on their own, establish its vertical position within the mineralizing system. Further structural, mineralogical and geochemical evaluation, together with drilling, is required to test the potential for additional mineralization and higher-grade gold zones at depth. Next Steps in Exploration Diamond drilling. Thirteen core holes over 1,037.40 m have been completed at Diana, El Rincón-Bellotoso and El Batamote. Eleven were drilled for metallurgical testwork, including two short restarts, and two for exploration at El Batamote and at Diana. Step-out drilling. RC drilling continues west and northwest of Diana toward El Batamote and southwest across the Bellotoso Plateau toward the proposed open-pit mining operation. The drilling will test potential extensions of gold mineralization along north-northwest-trending vein corridors, including structures associated with historic workings. Northern concessions. articles.title: American Fusion Inc. (OTCQB: AMFN) Announces Independent Third-Party Texatron™ Technology Review and Anticipated North Texas Ranch Facility Acquisition
articles.description: Independent reviewer conducting on-site evaluation through November 10; Company anticipates final report before the end of November and Ranch Facility closing before Thanksgiving SOUTHLAKE, Texas, Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- American Fusion Inc. (OTCQB: AMFN) ("American Fusion” or the "Company”), developer of the proprietary Texatron™ Fusion Engine™, today announced two developments in the advancement of its fusion technology program and North Texas research and development infrastructure. Independent Third-Party Technology Review Underway American Fusion is currently undergoing an independent third-party technology review of its proprietary Texatron™ fusion energy platform. The independent reviewer is conducting an on-site evaluation at the Company’s facilities, with the visit scheduled to continue through Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The review represents an important step in the Company’s ongoing efforts to obtain independent technical assessment of its fusion technology, engineering development and progress toward future testing and commercialization objectives. Following completion of the on-site evaluation, the Company anticipates receiving the independent reviewer’s final report before the end of November 2026, subject to completion of the review process. American Fusion intends to provide additional information regarding the findings and availability of the report once finalized. The Company believes independent technical evaluation is an important component of establishing credibility with prospective institutional investors, strategic partners, engineering organizations and potential commercial customers. "Having an independent third party conduct an on-site technology review is an important milestone for American Fusion,” said Brent Nelson, Chairman and CEO of American Fusion. "We welcome independent scrutiny of our Texatron™ technology and our engineering program. Our objective is to demonstrate our progress through a disciplined process of technical evaluation, testing and independent assessment. We look forward to receiving the reviewer’s final report later this month.” The review remains in progress, and its conclusions will not be known until the independent reviewer completes the assessment and issues its report. The review should not be interpreted as certification of commercial performance or validation of any particular technical claim. Anticipated Closing of North Texas Ranch Facility Before Thanksgiving American Fusion also announced that it expects to complete the acquisition of its planned Ranch Facility in North Texas before Thanksgiving Day, November 26, 2026, subject to completion of customary closing requirements. The Ranch Facility is intended to become a key component of the Company’s long-term North Texas operations, providing a dedicated location for the continued development of the Texatron™ technology and the expansion of its engineering, research, testing and assembly capabilities. The planned facility is expected to support the Company’s strategy of establishing a permanent operational campus capable of accommodating future technology development and testing infrastructure as the engineering program advances. "Closing on our Ranch Facility will represent another important step in building the permanent foundation for American Fusion,” Nelson continued. "Our vision is to establish a dedicated North Texas campus where our engineering teams can develop, assemble, evaluate and ultimately demonstrate our fusion energy systems. We believe that having a permanent facility is essential to supporting a serious, long-term technology development and commercialization program.” The Company anticipates providing shareholders with additional information regarding the property acquisition, facility development plans and future operational milestones following the closing. Advancing the Texatron™ Development Program The independent technology review and anticipated Ranch Facility acquisition represent complementary elements of American Fusion’s development strategy. The Company continues to pursue independent technical assessment of its Texatron™ platform while establishing the physical infrastructure intended to support expanded research, engineering and testing activities. "November is shaping up to be an important month for American Fusion,” Nelson concluded. "We are focused on measurable technical progress, independent evaluation and establishing the facilities necessary to execute our long-term business plan. We believe these developments are important steps in positioning American Fusion for the next phase of its development.” About American Fusion Inc. American Fusion Inc.
